facts.text: Sugar City was chartered in 1903 and incorporated in 1906, establishing Idaho's first company town for sugar beet processing.
Sugar City sprang up as a company town for the Fremont County Sugar Company, with a sugar beet factory built between 1903 and 1904.
Because early workers lived in tents, Sugar City earned the nickname 'Rag Town' before the factory’s first buildings appeared.
A labor shortage at the factory attracted Nikkei Japanese migrants, creating a lasting Japanese-American community in Sugar City.
The sugar factory shut down in 1942 after producing 405,000 tons of sugar beet, marking the end of Sugar City’s industrial era.
Union Pacific’s arrival connected Sugar City to national markets, enabling trade of sugar, livestock, grains, potatoes, and timber.
